info.name: Nahata Sports - Admin Panel - Reports & Analytics API
info.description:
Every API behind **Dashboard > Reports & Analytics** in the admin panel
(`/reports`), plus the drill-down modals it opens.

---

## Base URL
Set the `baseUrl` collection variable - it already ends in `/api`.
- Local: `http://localhost:5050/api`
- Production: confirm the API host with the backend team

---

## Auth
1. Run **00 - Auth > Login (Admin)** first; its test script stores the tokens.
2. Everything else inherits `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`.

The admin panel logs in with `portal: "admin"` - only `ADMIN` and
`COMPLEX_ADMIN` may use it.

---

## Who sees what
Every `/reports/*` route requires a token AND one of `ADMIN`,
`COMPLEX_ADMIN`, `EMPLOYEE`. `COACH` and `USER` are rejected at the router.

| Role | Scope | Coach share / Nahata turnover |
|---|---|---|
| ADMIN | All complexes, plus a per-complex breakdown | Yes |
| COMPLEX_ADMIN | Pinned to their own complex | Yes |
| EMPLOYEE | Pinned to their own complex | **No** - omitted from the payload, not just hidden |

A scoped caller cannot widen their scope: passing `sportComplexId` only ever
narrows a super admin's view, and is overridden for everyone else.

---

## Dates
Every range-aware endpoint takes plain `startDate` / `endDate` (`yyyy-mm-dd`).
The API widens them to `00:00:00` and `23:59:59.999` of those local days, so -
unlike some other modules - you do NOT append a time to `endDate` here.
Omit both for all-time (`period.allTime === true`).

The page's dropdown maps to: `7days`, `30days`, `90days`, `1year`, `custom`.
Chart endpoints additionally accept that keyword as `range`, but explicit
dates always win.

---

## Screen to endpoint

| UI element | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| Header stat cards + trend badges | `GET /reports/overview` |
| Total Turnover / Coach Share / Nahata Turnover + Turnover by Complex | `GET /reports/turnover` |
| Coaching / Court / Event cards -> **View in Detail** | `GET /reports/turnover/breakdown` |
| **Export Excel** | `GET /reports/export/excel` (streams .xlsx) |
| Booking trends / Revenue by court / Peak hours charts | `GET /reports/booking-trends`, `/revenue-by-court`, `/peak-hours` |
| Court performance table + its court filter | `GET /reports/court-performance` |
| Bookings modal | `GET /reports/bookings/filter-options`, `/bookings/all` |
| Students modal | `GET /reports/students/filter-options`, `/students/all` |
| New Students modal | `GET /reports/students/new/filter-options`, `/students/new` |
| Coaches modal | `GET /reports/coaches/filter-options`, `/coaches/all` |
| Coach Retention card + modal | `GET /reports/coaches/retention` |

---

## Response envelope
```json
{ "success": true, "data": { } }
```
Errors add `message` and `error`. The Excel export is the one exception - it
returns a binary body.

## Status codes
| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | OK |
| 401 | Missing / expired token, or the account is disabled |
| 403 | Role not allowed on `/reports/*` (COACH, USER) |
| 500 | Server error - `error` carries the detail |

Note: every read here is defensive - a failing chart query returns an empty
array rather than a 500, so an empty chart is not proof the request failed.

page title.

request.description:
Counts + trend badges for the range. Returns `data` with:

`totalUsers`, `totalStudents`, `newStudentsCount`, `newStudentsPercentage`,
`activeMemberships`, `totalBookings`, `totalRevenue`, `todayBookings`,
`upcomingBookings`, `activeEnrollments`, `activeSportsComplexes`, `totalCourts`,
`totalCoaches`, `period { startDate, endDate, comparedToStart }`,
`periodCounts { bookings, bookingsPrior, students, ..., revenue, revenuePrior }`
and the badge pairs `revenueChange` / `revenueTrendIsNew`, `bookingsTrend` /
`bookingsTrendIsNew`, `studentsTrend`, `usersTrend`, `coachesTrend`.

`*TrendIsNew` = there was no baseline in the prior period, so render **New**
instead of a fake +100%. That is the "compared with the previous period of the
same length" line under the page title.

`totalUsers` is website-wide and NOT complex-scoped (Active accounts only);
everything else is scoped.

request.description:
Feeds **TOTAL TURNOVER**, **TOTAL COACH SHARE** and **NAHATA TURNOVER**, plus the
TURNOVER BY COMPLEX table underneath.

```
data = {
  period: { startDate, endDate, allTime },
  scope: 'all' | 'complex',  sportComplexId,
  totalTurnover,
  bySource: { coaching, court, event },   // the 3 drill-down cards
  byComplex: [ { sportComplexId, name, city, totalTurnover, bySource,
                 coachShare, nahataTurnover } ],
  coachShare, nahataTurnover, diagnostics, reconciles   // ADMIN / COMPLEX_ADMIN only
}
```

**Role visibility** - an `EMPLOYEE` gets Total Turnover only; `coachShare`,
`nahataTurnover`, `diagnostics` and `reconciles` are omitted from the payload
entirely, not merely hidden in the UI.

`byComplex` is only built for an unscoped caller (super admin). A COMPLEX_ADMIN
gets `[]` because their whole payload already is their complex.

`reconciles` asserts `nahataTurnover + coachShare === totalTurnover` - if it ever
comes back false, the figures disagree and `diagnostics` says where.

Omit both dates for an all-time figure (`period.allTime === true`).

request.description:
Behind **View in Detail** on all three source cards. ONE call returns all three
trees, so the modal switches source and expands a node with no round trip - and
the Excel export builds every sheet from the same snapshot, so the workbook can
never mix data read at two different instants.

```
data = {
  period, scope, sportComplexId,
  totals: { court, coaching, event, total },
  sources: {
    court:    { key, label, hint, levels: ['Complex','Sport','Court'],
                countLabel: 'Bookings', hasCoachShare: false, total, nodes: [] },
    coaching: { levels: ['Complex','Sport','Coach'], countLabel: 'Students',
                hasCoachShare, total, coachShare, nahataRevenue, nodes: [] },
    event:    { levels: ['Complex','Event','Pass / Slot'], countLabel: 'Passes',
                total, nodes: [] }
  }
}
```

Each node is `{ id, name, subtitle, count, revenue, children[] }`, three levels
deep. For coaching, nodes also carry `coachShare` / `nahataRevenue` - stripped
recursively for an `EMPLOYEE`, along with `hasCoachShare: false`.

Coaching money is dated by when it was **recorded** (`FeePayments.paidOn`), so a
month renewal lands in the month it was collected, not the month the enrolment
row was created.

request.description:
The green **Export Excel** button. Streams a four-sheet `.xlsx` built server-side:
**Summary**, **Court Booking**, **Coaching**, **Events** - the full hierarchy and
every line item behind it, not just what the page happens to have fetched.

Not a JSON endpoint. In Postman use **Send and Download**; in code request it as
a blob (`responseType: 'blob'`).

Response headers: `Content-Type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.
spreadsheetml.sheet`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="..."`, and
`Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Content-Disposition` - without that last one a
cross-origin XHR cannot read the filename the server chose.

`rangeLabel` is cosmetic: it is printed inside the workbook ("Last 30 Days",
"Custom range", ...). The coach-share columns are omitted for an `EMPLOYEE`.

Note: once the workbook starts streaming the API cannot switch to a JSON error,
so a mid-stream failure ends the response early rather than returning a 500 body.

Called once with NO filters on page load to feed the retention summary card; the
modal re-fetches the same endpoint with its own filters (see folder 03).

Defaults to the current month when `month` is omitted.

item.name: 03 - Drill-down modals
item.description:
Each modal loads its filter options once, then pages the list. All are
complex-scoped; `sportComplexId` narrows a super admin's view and is
overridden for anyone already scoped.

request.description:
Fills the Bookings modal's dropdowns.
`data = { sources: ['Website','Admin','Khelomore',...], complexes: [{id,name,city}],
sports: [{id,name}] }`.

A COMPLEX_ADMIN only ever sees their own complex in `complexes`.

query.description: Super admin only - narrows, never widens.
One of the values from filter-options.

request.description:
`data = { bookings: [...], total, page, totalPages }`, 20 per page in the UI,
ordered by date then start time, newest first.

**`sportComplexId` cannot widen scope** - a COMPLEX_ADMIN's own complex always
wins over whatever the param says. It only narrows for a super admin.

Only revenue-bearing bookings are counted (the same filter the turnover figures
use), so cancelled/unpaid rows do not appear.

`data = { batches: [{id, name, schedule, days, sportComplexId, sport, sportComplex}],
complexes: [{id,name,city}], statuses: ['Active','Inactive','Graduated','Transferred'] }`.

query.description: Super admin only - narrows, never widens.
Active | Inactive | Graduated | Transferred.

request.description:
`data = { students: [...], total, page, totalPages }`, ordered by enrollment date
descending.

Students are scoped through the batches they are enrolled in, so a complex filter
forces the batch join to be required and out-of-complex students drop out.

`data = { batches, complexes, sports }`. Also used by the Coach Retention modal -
the two share one filter bar.

query.description: 1-12. Defaults to the current month.
continued | discontinued.

request.description:
`data = { students: [...], total, page, totalPages, retentionRate,
enrolledLastMonth, continuedThisMonth }`.

Retention Rate (%) = students continued this month / students enrolled last
month x 100.

Every student row carries a `continued` flag (true when their status is still
`Active`). `retentionRatio=continued` filters to Active students,
`discontinued` to everyone else.
`data = { batches: [{id, name, sport}] }` - the Coaches modal only filters by batch.

`data = { coaches: [...], total, page, totalPages, totalStudents, totalRevenue }`.

Each coach carries `Batches[]` (id, name, fees, currentStudents, sport) plus a
derived `totalStudents` and `totalRevenue`.

**Caveat**: `totalRevenue` here is `currentStudents x batch fees` - a *potential*
figure computed from active batches, NOT money actually collected. Use
`/reports/turnover/breakdown` (coaching tree) for real collected coaching revenue.

Filtering by `batchId` drops coaches who have no matching batch, and `total` then
reflects the filtered count rather than the raw query count.

query.description: 1-12. Defaults to the current month.
continued | discontinued.

request.description:
"Which coach keeps their students?" for a chosen month M.

- `base` = students whose enrolment in that coach's batch was live in **M-1**
- `retained` = of those, still live in M (enrolment still valid, or they
  re-enrolled with the same coach during M)
- `dropped` = base - retained, `retentionRate` = retained / base x 100

```
data = {
  month, monthLabel, previousMonth, previousMonthLabel,
  overall: { coaches, coachesWithBase, base, retained, dropped, newJoiners,
             activeThisMonth, retentionRate, bestCoach },
  coaches: [ { coachId, coachName, email, phone, sportComplex, sports[],
               batchCount, base, retained, dropped, newJoiners, activeThisMonth,
               retentionRate, students[] } ]
}
```

"Live in month X" uses the enrolment's own window (enrollmentDate -> validTill,
falling back to the batch end date, a missing end meaning ongoing) - the same rule
the coach panel's Student Enrollments screen uses, so the two never disagree.

Coaches are sorted best-retention first, and a coach with no base sinks below a
real 5/5 rather than outranking it on a 0/0. Passing `retentionRatio` also drops
coaches left with no matching students.
